chunks: And Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:
"Indeed, the last salat (prayer) that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله led with the people was in a single garment, having crossed its two ends. Shall I show you the garment?"
He said: then he brought out a cloak, and I measured it, and it was seven cubits by eight hand spans.

key_terms.أَشْبَارٍ: hand spans, a unit of measurement
key_terms.بِالنَّاسِ: with the people, meaning in congregation
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ: a single garment worn during prayer
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.صَلَاةٍ: salat (prayer), specifically the act of ritual worship being described
key_terms.طَرَفَيْهِ: its two ends, referring to the ends of the garment
key_terms.مِلْحَفَةً: a cloak or wrap that was brought out

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith show about praying in a single garment in congregation?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed his final congregational salat (prayer) wearing a single garment, with its ends crossed. The report preserves a practical detail about the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم manner of dress in prayer and indicates the sufficiency of such a garment in congregational worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1134 – Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said:
"The last prayer that the Messenger of Allah (sw) led the people in was while wearing a single garment, with its ends crossed over one another. Shall I show you the garment?"
He then brought out a cloak, and I measured it—it was seven cubits by eight hand spans.
